analysis: The only change in ProviderLoop.swift is in the add-on hold state block (head lines 493-502). It adds `addonHoldSettleTimeout`, initialized from `ProviderLoop.addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault`. It also adds the internal test hook `addonHoldBeforeCancellingStragglersForTesting`, which is nil in production. The base doc comment is reworded. These are stored properties on the actor and add no new input parsing, IPC surface, authentication change, crypto or persistence. They don't touch the coordinator wire, attestation, App Attest authorization, prefix-cache storage (T-041) or key custody. The relevant threat is T-059 (TB-012, A-018), a local process holding the provider out of routing. The new settle timeout is a bound on the hold drain/settle sequence. It is plausibly availability-positive, but the visible diff does not show how it is consumed. The test hook is internal and unset in production. It lets a test suspend the drain's straggler-cancellation pass, but it is not reachable by an external adversary. The static `addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault` is not in the supplied evidence, so its value is unverified. The companion files (`ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift`, `AddonIPCServer`) were not supplied. The next pass should check three things there: whether the settle timeout is bounded so a same-UID holder cannot extend the hold or the unload indefinitely, whether the straggler-cancellation race with a release cannot leave a stale hold or routing state, and whether the peer-signature check and lease handling are unchanged. No concrete regression is identifiable from this file alone.
